BiblicalUsage: The word is the Aramaic word for a vessel, and it is the word of the temple's stolen gold. Belshazzar commanded the golden and silver vessels his father had taken out of the temple in Jerusalem to be brought, so the king and his princes and wives and concubines might drink from them, and that same night the writing appeared on the wall. Cyrus took the vessels out of the temple of Babylon and delivered them to Sheshbazzar, and Darius decreed they should be restored to the temple at Jerusalem, every one to his place.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the vessels teach us that holy things are not safe in profane hands, and God writes judgment on the wall the night they are misused. I hold that the same vessels came home again, because what men steal from God's house, God restores to His house in His own time.
